fulltext: IT之家 9 月 9 日消息，铠侠公司 CEO 太田裕雄在接受彭博社采访时明确否认了与其竞争对手兼股东 SK 海力士深化合作的可能性，同时承诺抑制飙升的存储芯片价格，以避免损害长期 AI 需求。
近期，存储芯片制造商正进行大规模产能扩张以满足 AI 服务提供商的订单需求，价格出现两位数甚至三位数的涨幅。SK 集团董事长崔泰源本月初在接受《朝日新闻》采访时，曾将铠侠与 SK 海力士之间的制造合作列为一项可选方案。
然而，太田裕雄表示，与 SK 海力士加强合作的方案将面临反垄断障碍，并且难以与铠侠和闪迪共同拥有的制造设施相协调。针对铠侠、SK 海力士和闪迪三家公司联合生产的假设，他回应称：“我们不能就这样说，‘好吧，那就让三家公司一起合作吧’。我们完全不知道崔泰源为何发表那样的言论。”
市场对两家公司深化合作的猜测升温，源于双方正在合作开发非易失性磁性存储器，且铠侠部分固态硬盘所使用的 DRAM 芯片由 SK 海力士供应。此外，SK 海力士还持有可转换为铠侠 14.19% 股权的债券。
价格方面，铠侠 NAND 闪存平均价格在截至 6 月的季度中环比上涨 70%，此前一季度价格涨幅已超过一倍。今年 4 月就任 CEO 的太田裕雄表示，已指示销售团队不要向数据中心运营商大幅提高价格，以免损害 AI 领域的投资意愿。他称“价格已经涨得够高了”，并表示芯片价格不太可能再出现环比上涨 70% 的情况，“即使是超大规模云服务商，预算也是有限的”。
公开资料显示，铠侠股价较一年前上涨了 18 倍，6 月曾一度超越软银集团和丰田汽车成为日本市值最高的公司，随后因市场担忧产能过剩、债务水平上升及 AI 领域竞争激烈而有所回落。
铠侠与闪迪计划共同投入超过 5 万亿日元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,184.7 亿元人民币）扩大其位于日本工厂的生产能力。太田裕雄表示，铠侠不会“为了市场份额而追逐市场份额”，而是会努力提供企业客户优先寻求的技术。

cards.title: 宜宾，一场机器人“招聘会”的产业雄心
cards.summary: 9月3日，宜宾国际会展中心，55支机器人团队正在完成一场特殊的“面试”。
fulltext: 9月3日，宜宾国际会展中心，55支机器人团队正在完成一场特殊的“面试”。
江源之水，终向大海。
9月3日，宜宾国际会展中心。世界动力电池大会的聚光灯下，55支机器人团队正在完成一场特殊的“面试”。
应聘者是机器人。考官是产线。考题是真实任务，覆盖产线搬运、物品配送、衣物整理、饮品制作、应急救援等场景。130余支团队报名，横跨工业、商业、生活娱乐、开放创新四大赛道。
这就是“江源杯”2026具身智能场景技能挑战赛。但，如果你只把它看作一场比赛，就看轻了。
参赛团队带来的不是PPT，是实机；产业方追问的不是创意概念，是报价、交付周期和定制空间。清智资本已推动两个项目在宜宾完成场景对接与试点落地。
一场比赛变成了招聘会。赛场变成了POC验证现场。奖杯变成了订单。汇江向海，逐立上游。
当行业还在争论人形机器人何时规模化落地，宜宾已经让机器人在产线上“应聘上岗”了。
长江自雪域高原奔腾而下，在宜宾汇流三江。两千年前，这里是僰道古渡；近代以降，这里是西南运输的命脉。码头文化里浸透一种精神：不务虚、不炫技，只看货物能不能过得了江、到得了岸。老船工看一眼吃水线，就知道船能不能扛住险滩。
这种务实基因，一脉相承到了今天。当年验船看吃水线，今天验机器人看产线。
展台上翻跟头、视频里叠衣服，每一次亮相都能收获掌声和流量。但一个尴尬的现实是：出了展馆，绝大多数机器人连工厂车间里的一个工位都顶不上去。
产线上的光照变化，能让视觉系统瞬间失灵。机械振动，能让惯性测量单元产生漂移。狭窄的操作空间，能让多轴协同变成相互打架。通用能力演示与具体产业需求之间，横亘着一道真实的鸿沟。而展台上的掌声，填不平它。
这道沟的形成，源于三层结构性缺口。
第一层，场景虚化。多数赛事和展示停留在标准化环境。机器人在实验室里“会走”，但进不了工厂。面对非结构化产线、动态干扰、多品种小批量，实验室的高光表现迅速褪色。
第二层，数据饥渴。一个机器人要在工厂真正“上岗”，需要的不是静态数据集，而是在真实产线上与人、设备、物料反复交互形成的动态决策模型。没有20万小时级实景数据打底，所谓的“自主学习”只是空中楼阁。
第三层，验证缺位。从论文到产品之间，还隔着一道POC的鸿沟。高校有算法但缺场景，企业有场景但缺技术，资本有耐心但缺标准。产学研之间，欠缺一套让技术、场景、资本三方在同一套规则下对话的机制。
“江源杯”的解题思路，正是从这三重缺口切入。大赛共设置了工业、商业、生活娱乐、开放创新四大赛道，分别有71支、44支、32支、66支队伍报名参赛。赛题不出自专家组的头脑风暴，而是从宜宾本地企业的产线上直接“长”出来的。

工业赛道下设三个项目，直接对准工厂最硬核的痛点。产线搬运上料，对应酒厂粮袋搬运、汽车产线来料分拣等真实场景，考核重载搬运稳定性。零件分拣与装配，对应3C产线电路板组装等场景，机器人需依BOM从混料盘识别不同颜色、形状、姿态的零件，完成分拣、翻转校正、夹具定位、螺丝锁付和成品摆放，夹具定位销误差要求≤0.1mm——约一根发丝粗细。工业厂区巡检，对应化工园区巡检等场景，考核多传感器融合感知与巡检闭环。
商业赛道模拟的是园区配送与展厅导览。比如配送机器人要在平地、砂石、坡道、台阶等复合地形中完成载荷运输，考核多地形自适应通行与动态避障。生活娱乐赛道则力求还原日常场景，球类运动、衣物整理、早餐制作、桌面整理、饮品制作等，核心围绕柔性操作、精细抓取与自主决策。
开放创新赛道则完全放开，由参赛方自主自选方向：应急救援、农林作业、水下探测、特种巡检、文旅创意。一些团队则瞄准了那些多年被认为“无法自动化”的硬骨头。消防机器人便是其一。火场之中，凭借80kg 动态负载与 200kg 静态承压，可背负整套消防装备负重 60kg 连续爬楼 50 层，稳扛高压水炮80L/s超120 斤后坐力。
这些考题的背后，站着120余家动力电池上下游企业、光伏组件车间、储能电站和白酒酿造工坊。宜宾把全域产业场景开放出来，全部变成了机器人的“考场”。
底层逻辑只有一个：机器人不是来表演的，是来应聘上岗的。就像当年的老船工，不看船造得多漂亮，只看它能不能过江。
全国130余支团队报名参赛，像支流汇入长江。带着算法、带着样机、带着对真实场景的渴望，奔赴一个正在形成的产业磁场。
这场“招聘会”最精妙的设计，在于赛事本身就是一个完整的验证闭环。

赛事同步嵌入世界动力电池大会的生态展览。银河通用、优必选、智平方、极佳、跨维等头部企业携核心产品亮相，50余家参赛企业同台竞技，展品覆盖机器人整机、核心芯片、算力、数据采集装备，从本体到核心零部件再到数据层方案，形成具身智能全产业链的集中展示。世界动力电池大会展览面积达5万平方米，汇聚全球超2000家企业、30余国800余名嘉宾、5万名专业观众。这不是一个孤立的赛场，而是一个嵌入全球产业链的产业入口。
但真正的“杀招”是产业路演。这边机器人刚比完分拣，隔壁展台就有企业负责人拿着名片来问报价和交付周期。那边路演刚结束，投资机构的合作意向书就递了过来。赛场边的空气里，飘着的不是硝烟，是合作的信号。
清智资本已有两个项目在宜宾完成场景对接与试点落地：泡茶机器人对接川茶集团产业场景开展试点验证；智能具身硬件自动化设计平台联动本地高校开设了课程，从源头培养产业人才。
机器人在赛场里拿到的不是奖牌，而是实实在在的订单、合作意向和落地场景。赛场与市场，仅一墙之隔。
真实场景的价值还不止于验证，更在于数据回流。
西南具身智能训练中心已于2025年9月正式投入运营，在全国同类城市中率先跑通了从需求对接到服务交付的市场化运营闭环，构建起“数据采集—模型训练—场景落地”的一体化能力。按照规划，2026年其专业数据采集运营团队将突破500人规模，部署各类数据采集机器人超过250台，目标产出超过20万小时的高质量、多模态机器人交互数据集。
一年20万小时的实景交互数据，意味着什么？机器人在这里“训练”，不是在模拟器里跑虚拟场景，而是在真实工厂、真实仓库、真实商业空间里与真实的人和设备交互。就像江水冲刷河床，每一次交互都在塑造更坚韧的“河床”，让机器人的决策模型在真实世界的摩擦力中日益精进。
数据飞轮一旦运转起来，便会形成越赛越强、越强越赛的正向循环：赛事产生真实场景需求，场景产生高质量数据，数据反哺参赛团队优化算法，优化后的算法在下一轮赛事中接受更严苛的验证。每一轮，都在为中国具身智能产业积累最稀缺的“实战经验”。
宜宾在此扮演的角色，则是一个“超级链接器”。让技术供给方和产业需求方面对面，当场验证、当场洽谈、当场转化。
机器人企业不远千里来到宜宾参赛，绝不只是因为这里有一场赛。真正吸引它们的，是这座城市在长江上游积蓄了十年的“水位”——场景、资本、数据、人才，四股要素在此汇流，到了自然外溢的时候。
大约十年前，宜宾还以白酒和煤炭闻名。随后宁德时代落地，动力电池产业链从零建立，规上工业总产值连续三年突破千亿元，产量占全国约六分之一。紧接着是晶硅光伏，一年时间引入四家头部企业，39家配套跟进，产业规模做到全省第一。然后是新型储能、智能网联新能源汽车。
每一步都不快，但每一步都扎实。就像长江上游的江水，不急不缓，但从不回头。
复盘这套打法，核心逻辑清晰可见：看准产业趋势，引入龙头企业，用资本撬动配套，用场景验证产品，最终形成完整的产业生态。龙头企业是源头活水，基金是支流汇入，场景是河床塑形，人才是两岸青山。四者相互作用，自然成势。
如今这套“龙头带动、基金招商、场景验证、生态赋能”的方法论，正被完整地迁移到具身智能赛道上。
这不是从零开始。动力电池的电池管理系统、精密结构件和能源控制技术，与机器人核心部件高度同源。智能网联汽车积累的传感器、自动驾驶和车规级制造经验，可直接迁移到机器人的感知与运动控制领域。从招商谈判到园区管理、从政策设计到政企协同，一整套被多个新能源项目打磨过的产业服务能力，正在被无缝复用。
方法论跑通了，但还需要场景、资本、数据、人才四要素在此就位，才能验证它确实可迁移。

最大的底气，来自场景的富集度。全球最大的动力电池产业集群就在家门口，从电芯、正负极材料到隔膜、电解液的完整产业链，120余家上下游企业汇聚，产能规划接近300GWh。高度自动化的锂电工厂、光伏组件车间、储能电站、新能源汽车产线，这些已经跑通的智能生产场景，本身就是机器人最理想的试验场。四川时代基地先后获得全球灯塔工厂、可持续灯塔、零碳工厂认证，是锂电行业少有的同时拿到三项荣誉的生产基地。在这里，机器人不是“找场景”，而是“被场景追着跑”。
资本已经就位。宜宾联合中移资本、金沙江联合资本等机构设立了8只AI方向基金，总规模30亿元，已投资20余家机器人相关企业。

数据正在产出。西南具身智能训练中心已投入运营，头部企业已在此扎堆开展后训练与实景采集；银河通用西南具身智能制造基地同步落地，整机制造与量产能力已就位。以银河通用为链主，整机与核心零部件制造正在集聚，力争本地配套率达60%左右；与华翔启源、均普智能等龙头共建的打样中心与柔性产线已落地，推动具身智能产品实现全流程闭环。与此同时，宜宾正聚焦“人工智能+场景”，开放“山湖天地”“菜坝文旅新城”等高价值应用场景推动行业大模型落地；布局AIDC新兴赛道，以分布式算力节点牵引运营商落地，聚焦液冷系统与HVDC方向招引制造类企业，打造AIDC设备制造与POC验证基地。
算力具备成本优势。本地丰富的水电资源支撑起低成本的分布式算力布局，这是沿海城市很难复制的能源优势。
人才形成供给。 14所高校、10万在校大学生。宜宾人工智能科技园的人才公寓入住率达95%以上，数字经济社区配套宿舍入住率超80%。人来了，留得住。
四要素在此汇流，不是偶然，是方法论驱动下的必然结果。就像长江从不停留在宜宾，但它总是在这里把各路支流汇成一股更大的力量，然后奔涌向东。
而“江源杯”，恰好是这套方法论在AI赛道自然延伸的一次精准落子。它是宜宾在长江上游积蓄了十年产业势能之后，自然外溢的一次奔流。水到渠成，仅此而已。
赛事的终点，是产业落地的起点。
“江源杯”的价值，远不止于决出胜负。它为行业提供了一套可复制的范式：以真实场景为考场，以POC验证为路径，以数据回流为闭环，让技术走出实验室有了清晰的路线图。
按照规划，到2028年，宜宾将培育3到5家千人规模的数据服务企业、5家以上具身智能链主企业，带动产值达100亿至150亿元，人工智能产业就业达2.5万人，形成高质量数据集100万小时。
这些数字并非空中楼阁。目前已有100余家数字经济企业落地，累计签约投资超230亿元。全市已谋划超120个机器人应用场景，将部署超千台机器人，涵盖引导配送、巡检协作、安防环卫、无人驾驶等多元领域。
而这座城市的野心，不止于产值。
机器人的“工位”，正在从动力电池产线向更广阔的产业场景延伸：白酒窖池边的智能酿造、城市道路的无人清扫、智慧园区的全天候巡检、康养中心的理疗服务、零售仓储的智能分拣。宜宾正在全域挖掘“高价值小切口”场景，推动首台套产品验证并逐步推广。
对于机器人企业而言，宜宾不只是一个参赛目的地，这里的真实场景能让技术变成产品，这里的产业生态能把产品变成生意。“江源杯”则验证了一种可能：让机器人走出实验室的最好方式，不是给它更大的展台，而是给它一份真实的“工作”。
江源之水，终向大海。从白酒到动力电池，从晶硅光伏到新型储能，再到具身智能，宜宾的每一步都踩在产业变革的节点上。汇江向海，逐立上游——这座城市的精神，从来不是守在源头，而是奔向大海。这一次，它选择用一场“招聘会”作为切口，让技术走出实验室，让机器人走进真实世界。
招聘会结束了，但上岗才刚刚开始。长江从不停留，宜宾也是。

On August 4, Grant De Swardt, an independent AI consultant in East Sussex, U.K., noticed something strange going on with his Claude Max 20x account. He hadn’t been working that day, yet his token usage was climbing.

The next day, he disabled everything he had attached to Claude and did not work with it. Token consumption again increased. “In the clearest controlled interval, it increased from 45% to 55% while I performed no work, scheduled Cowork tasks were paused or completed, Dispatch/cloud execution was disabled, and there was no corresponding active local Claude Code task,” De Swardt told TechCrunch.

What was eating up his token allowance? He had no idea, so he contacted Anthropic and asked for an itemized list. Anthropic didn’t provide one, but it agreed something was off. It suspended his paid account, invalidated all of his sessions and server-side Claude Code tokens, and issued him a partial refund of £44.49 for the remaining time on his $200-per-month subscription.

The suspension wreaked havok on his business, he told TechCrunch. His job is to help small and mid-size businesses set up agents — a sort of forward-deployed engineer for hire — for tasks like automatically loading purchase-order data from emails into the accounting software.
As a sole proprietor, he relies on agents throughout his whole business, too: daily admin tasks, website design, coding. “Like everything is just running through AI these days,” he said.

After investigating, Anthropic told De Swardt it found the culprit: A compromised Claude session key was used to mint unauthorized Claude Code OAuth tokens. The company told him the account “appeared to have been used by an unauthorized-looking third-party service to handle activity for other people, but they could not determine how it obtained access,” he told TechCrunch. “They say the evidence is consistent either with credentials/session data being taken without my knowledge, or with the account having been connected to an outside service.”

In other words, a hacker was able to obtain access to De Swardt’s account and was covertly siphoning off his tokens. Because account support tracks total usage but not itemized usage, even upon request, this kind of theft could have gone on for months undetected.

He posted his experience on Reddit and after 80 comments, he discovered he was not alone. One person claimed that their account “was auto-upgraded without my consent, my credit card got charged, and the usage shot from 0% to 100% automatically without me even touching it.” Another saw usage go from 0 to 49% in 12 minutes, when all they had used it for was a couple of prompts and a web search.

One Claude user said their account burned through its max tokens every day for three days without them using it at all; this person then created a GitHub report about it. Like with the Reddit post, other users shared similar experiences there, too.
Two of them posted emails from Anthropic where the company had — to its credit — identified and warned them that their tokens were being stolen.

“We have recently become aware of a bad actor that is using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions from people’s computers, then using those login sessions to access Claude accounts and consume their usage,” the email read. Infostealers are a type of malware that installs itself on a user’s computer and steals saved passwords, session data, and login credentials.
When Anthropic saw suspicious activity, it signed the users out, invalidated existing authorizations, issued some refunds, and warned them that they may have malware.
The company also said the malware didn’t come from using Claude itself. Such malware can be picked up from many sources online, from downloading infected software to clicking on infected ads.
Anthropic did not send De Swardt one of those emails. He insists he found no evidence that his computer was compromised and says he still has no way of determining how hackers gained access.

De Swardt’s Claude account was reinstated after about two weeks. But the difficulty of getting speedy help for the matter, plus the lack of an itemized usage, soured him on Claude. He cancelled his subscription in favor of Cursor and its ability to use multiple models, including more affordable open source options.

In his experience, these other models work as well as Claude. “It’s not that much different or better,” he said, adding that he can’t see going back “without [Anthropic] actually having resolved the issue in any way.”
He says Anthropic still lacks tools that allow users to see what’s consuming their tokens. “I don’t think there’s any way that these people can protect themselves.”
When asked for information on how users can identify misuse, Anthropic declined to comment.

8月4日，英国东萨塞克斯的独立人工智能顾问Grant De Swardt注意到他的Claude Max 20x账户发生了一些奇怪的事情。那天他没有工作，但他的代币使用量正在攀升。
第二天，他禁用了克劳德所拥有的一切，并且没有使用它。代币消耗量再次增加。De Swardt告诉TechCrunch ： “在最清晰的受控时间间隔内，它从45 ％增加到55 ％ ，而我没有执行任何工作，计划的Cowork任务暂停或完成，调度/云执行被禁用，并且没有相应的活动本地Claude Code任务。”
是什么吞噬了他的象征性津贴？他不知道，所以他联系了Anthropic ，要求提供一份详细的清单。Anthropic没有提供，但它同意有些不对劲。它暂停了他的付费帐户，使他的所有会话和服务器端Claude Code令牌无效，并向他发放了44.49 £的部分退款，用于他的每月200 $订阅的剩余时间。
他告诉TechCrunch ，停职对他的生意造成了严重破坏。他的工作是帮助中小型企业设立代理商（一种前沿部署的雇佣工程师） ，以完成自动将采购订单数据从电子邮件加载到会计软件等任务。
作为独资经营者，他在整个业务中也依赖于代理商：日常管理任务、网站设计、编码。“就像现在一切都在通过人工智能一样，”他说。

经过调查， Anthropic告诉De Swardt ，它找到了罪魁祸首：一个被泄露的Claude会话密钥被用来铸造未经授权的Claude Code OAuth令牌。该公司告诉他，该帐户“似乎被未经授权的第三方服务用于为其他人处理活动，但他们无法确定它是如何获得访问权限的，”他告诉TechCrunch。“他们说，证据要么与在我不知情的情况下获取的凭据/会话数据一致，要么与已连接到外部服务的帐户一致。”
换句话说，一名黑客能够获得对De Swardt帐户的访问权限，并秘密窃取他的代币。由于账号支持会跟踪总使用情况，但不会逐项记录使用情况，因此即使提出请求，此类盗窃也可能持续数月而未被发现。
他在Reddit上发布了自己的体验，在80条评论后，他发现自己并不孤单。一个人声称他们的账号“未经我同意而自动升级，我的信用卡被扣款，使用率从0%自动升级到100% ，我甚至没有碰过它。“另一个人在12分钟内看到使用率从0%上升到49% ，当时他们只使用了几个提示和网络搜索。
一位Claude用户表示，他们的帐户在三天内每天烧毁其最大代币，而他们根本没有使用它；此人随后创建了一个关于它的GitHub报告。与Reddit帖子一样，其他用户也在那里分享了类似的体验。
其中两人发布了来自Anthropic的电子邮件，该公司已经识别并警告他们的代币被盗。
“我们最近意识到一个恶意行为者正在使用常见的信息窃取恶意软件从人们的计算机上窃取Claude登录会话，然后使用这些登录会话访问Claude帐户并使用它们，”电子邮件读取。信息窃取者是一种恶意软件，它会自行安装在用户的计算机上，并窃取保存的密码、会话数据和登录凭据。
当Anthropic发现可疑活动时，它会将用户注销，使现有授权无效，发放了一些退款，并警告他们可能存在恶意软件。
该公司还表示，恶意软件并非来自使用Claude本身。从下载受感染的软件到点击受感染的广告，这些恶意软件可以从许多在线来源被发现。
Anthropic没有向De Swardt发送其中一封电子邮件。他坚称没有发现任何证据表明他的电脑遭到入侵，并表示他仍然无法确定黑客是如何获得访问权限的。
De Swardt的Claude帐户在大约两周后恢复。但是，很难得到迅速的帮助，加上缺乏一个逐项的用法，使他对克劳德感到不满。他取消了订阅，转而使用Cursor及其使用多种型号的能力，包括更实惠的开源选项。
根据他的经验，这些其他模型与克劳德一样有效。“这并没有太大的不同或更好，”他说，并补充说，如果[Anthropic]没有以任何方式实际解决问题，他就看不到回头路。
他说， Anthropic仍然缺乏允许用户查看其代币消费情况的工具。“我认为这些人无法保护自己。”
当被要求提供有关用户如何识别滥用的信息时， Anthropic拒绝发表评论。

Google recently rolled out its September Android Drop, introducing several new features to the platform. While it wasn’t available at the time, one of the new features that got announced was a new option in Find Hub designed to help you remember the locations of items that can’t be digitally tracked. The tech giant said the feature would be coming soon to devices running Android 16 or later. It seems the day for the rollout has now arrived.

The folks over at 9to5Google report that Find Hub’s new “Remembered” tab is here. It will join Devices and People as the third available option on the bottom bar. It is marked by a bookmark icon with a Gemini spark in the top right corner.

As suggested by the Gemini spark, you’ll be able to use Google’s AI to make a note on the location of any object, even if it’s not a connected device. There is also a floating action button (FAB) where you’ll find an “Ask Gemini” shortcut. Alternatively, you’ll be able to add objects to your Remembered tab manually.

If you decide to go the manual route, it will start off by requiring you to give the item a “Name” and “Storage spot.” After these steps are completed, you’ll be able to add more details. For example, you could add a picture, location details, and notes.

According to the outlet, the update appeared in version 3.1.732-02 of the Find Hub app. Although the update is available through the Google Play Store, it appears that the feature is not widely available quite yet.

A good smart home demands openness: With as many different devices as you’ll need to really get every last corner of your home automated, it’s critical that they all play nicely with each other. For Google Home, part of that means not arbitrarily setting up platform boundaries, and Google’s smart home solution is open for Apple users to enjoy. Unfortunately, Nest devices in particular have been experiencing a few hiccups lately when it comes to iOS devices — but Google’s already got good news.

We expect a few key features from any smart home setup — it needs to provide remote control through our devices, it should support automated actions, and it should notify us about things worth our attention. With Nest on iOS, however, users have reported running into trouble with that last one, sharing on sites like Reddit the problems they recently noticed with Nest notifications not coming through on iOS devices.

Impacted users share that the Nest app still seemed to be aware of all the notification events their smart home hardware delivered, and all could still be seen when manually pulling up the app. But as of a few days ago, those experiencing this glitch stopped receiving alerts when a new event took place.
Like we said, though, Google has some good news to share, and according to the company it’s both identified the underlying problem, and rolled out a fix:

By the sounds of it, there’s nothing for users to do themselves in order to start taking advantage of Google’s fix. Either everything important is happening on the back end, or Google’s silently pushing out an update.

Especially when we’re talking about things like Nest cameras, timely notifications are a big part of the appeal of these products — and risk even presenting a security risk when they’re broken. cards.title: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
cards.title_cn: 元押注AI特工Muse在人工智能竞赛中迎头赶上
cards.summary: 【Meta】Meta is making another push to bring artificial intelligence to the masses with Muse, a personal assistant it says can put AI in the hands of virtually anyone. The product is the latest step in a mult…
fulltext: Meta drills down on ease of use and privacy options after spending billions overhauling its AI strategy.

Meta is making another push to bring artificial intelligence to the masses with Muse, a personal assistant it says can put AI in the hands of virtually anyone. The product is the latest step in a multi-billion-dollar strategy overhaul designed to revitalize the company’s ailing position in the AI race and help it catch up to rivals like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

Muse is a “personal AI agent” designed to help out with everyday tasks and projects, like online shopping, sending emails, and planning a trip. Once given a goal, Meta says Muse can work on its own, opening a browser, filling out forms, and even negotiating on users’ behalf. For lengthy tasks, Meta says Muse will continue working in the background after users close the app, returning to users if something changes or if it requires approval for something, such as making a purchase.

Muse will roll out in the US on iOS, Android, and muse.ai, with AI glasses “coming soon.” The assistant will be free for most users, though Meta said there will be paid subscriptions “for people who want to do more.” The company did not specify the nature and costs of these paid plans, nor outline what limits there are for free users.
“Muse is a first step: an agent that takes on more of the work so people can focus on what matters to them,” Meta said.

While Meta is pitching Muse as “the world’s first personal AI agent built for everyone,” the product is, in fact, very similar to the growing array of AI assistants, teammates, and coworkers on offer from the company’s competitors. Most tools are indeed aimed at businesses or technically-minded individuals — notably OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work, Anthropic’s Claude Cowork, Microsoft’s Copilot Tasks, SpaceXAI’s Grok Bot, and the viral open-source agent Moltbot — though Google does appear to be targeting a similar audience with its recently-announced Gemini Spark assistant.

Ease of use is where Meta hopes Muse will stand out from the crowd. “Anyone can use it out of the box, no technical experience required,” Meta claims, boasting that “there’s no learning curve.” Communication is simple too, as easy as messaging the assistant through the Muse app or WhatsApp, one of Meta’s messaging platforms. It will also readily remember details users share, even if only mentioned once, Meta says, enabling it to make better and unprompted suggestions.

Meta is similarly keen to emphasize Muse’s privacy and security features. Securing trust will be key for making Muse actually useful as an AI assistant, as it will require a certain amount of personal information about each user to function effectively. With this in mind, Meta says people can opt out of their interactions being used to train Meta’s AI models (it’s not known whether this is on or off by default) and can instruct Muse to “forget” specific things it has learned about them.

Given their access to personal information and credentials like passwords and payment information, agents can naturally be a security and privacy nightmare. To keep data, passwords, and other information secure, Muse runs on a virtual computer in the cloud designed to keep data safe and separate from other users’ agents. It has no visibility into passwords or payment methods, Meta says, and another AI agent, Sentinel, patrols the same virtual machine to ensure nothing Muse does can reach the internet without approval.

Meta says it plans to introduce a more secure “confidential” version of the virtual machine later this year, encrypted so that even Meta cannot access it. 1Password and Shop Pay support are also on the way, the company said, adding that Muse can already checkout securely with Stripe’s Link.

Muse, powered by the company’s in-house model Muse Spark, is being positioned as the centerpiece of Meta’s AI strategy going forward as the company seeks to regain ground after years of setbacks and failures.

Given its position as a household name and social media behemoth, Meta is in a good position to reach many of these more casual users. But there is also no shortage of baggage for Meta to overcome. Trust-wise, it has just endured a grueling trial over the harms of social media and has faced numerous bruising privacy-related ordeals in the past, including the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Its AI overtures have also been plagued with missteps, including a “Discover” feature that displayed prompts, conversations, and image outputs from other users, a support chatbot that helped hackers take over more than 20,000 Instagram accounts, and a short-lived AI-generated clickbait news feed that appeared to break its own policies on AI content. There’s also its recent and unfortunate reputation for “pervert glasses.”

Meta正在通过Muse再次推动将人工智能带给大众， Muse是一名个人助理，据说可以将人工智能置于几乎任何人的手中。该产品是价值数十亿美元的战略改革中的最新一步，旨在重振该公司在人工智能竞赛中的不利地位，并帮助其赶上OpenAI、Anthropic和Google等竞争对手。

Muse将在美国推出iOS、Android和muse.ai ， AI眼镜“即将推出。大多数用户都可以免费使用该助手，但Meta表示，“对于想要做更多事情的人”，将提供付费订阅。“该公司没有具体说明这些付费计划的性质和成本，也没有概述免费用户的限制。
Meta说： “Muse是第一步：一个承担更多工作的代理，这样人们就可以专注于对他们来说重要的事情。”

虽然Meta将Muse称为“世界上第一个为所有人打造的个人AI代理” ，但实际上，该产品与公司竞争对手提供的越来越多的AI助手、队友和同事非常相似。大多数工具确实是针对企业或具有技术头脑的个人--尤其是OpenAI的ChatGPT Work、Anthropic的Claude Cowork、微软的Copilot Tasks、SpaceXAI的Grok Bot和病毒式开源代理Moltbot--尽管谷歌最近宣布的Gemini Spark助手似乎确实瞄准了类似的受众。

Meta同样热衷于强调Muse的隐私和安全功能。确保信任是使Muse真正成为人工智能助手的关键，因为它需要有关每个用户的一定数量的个人信息才能有效运作。考虑到这一点， Meta表示，人们可以选择不再使用他们的交互来训练Meta的人工智能模型（默认情况下不知道这是开启还是关闭） ，并可以指示Muse “忘记”它所了解的关于他们的具体内容。
由于代理可以访问个人信息和密码和付款信息等凭据，因此它们自然会成为安全和隐私的噩梦。为了确保数据、密码和其他信息的安全， Muse在云中的虚拟计算机上运行，旨在确保数据安全并与其他用户的代理分开。Meta说，它无法查看密码或付款方式，另一个人工智能代理Sentinel巡逻同一台虚拟机，以确保Muse在未经批准的情况下无法访问互联网。
Meta表示，它计划在今年晚些时候推出一个更安全的“机密”版本的虚拟机，经过加密，即使Meta也无法访问它。该公司表示， 1Password和Shop Pay的支持也正在进行中，并补充说， Muse已经可以通过Stripe的Link安全地结账。
Muse由该公司的内部模型Muse Spark提供支持，正被定位为Meta未来人工智能战略的核心，因为该公司在经历了多年的挫折和失败后寻求重新站稳脚跟。

鉴于其作为家喻户晓的名字和社交媒体巨头的地位， Meta处于一个很好的位置，可以接触到许多这些更随意的用户。但Meta也不乏需要克服的行李。从信任的角度来看，它刚刚经历了对社交媒体危害的艰苦考验，过去曾面临过许多与隐私相关的挫折，包括剑桥分析公司丑闻。它的人工智能提议也一直受到失误的困扰，包括显示其他用户提示、对话和图像输出的“发现”功能，帮助黑客接管2万多个Instagram帐户的支持聊天机器人，以及似乎违反了自己对人工智能内容政策的短暂人工智能生成的点击诱饵新闻提要。它最近还因“变态眼镜”而声名狼藉，令人遗憾。

cards.title: AI power users claim Anthropic duped them with subscriptions, and they’re taking it to court
cards.title_cn: 人工智能超级用户声称Anthropic通过订阅欺骗了他们，他们正在将其告上法庭
cards.summary: 【Anthropic】Anthropic says power users are key to its business - it's prioritized them even when it means cutting off other popular applications, like OpenClaw. But some of these same customers say Anthropic misl…
fulltext: Anthropic says power users are key to its business — it’s prioritized them even when it means cutting off other popular applications, like OpenClaw. But some of these same customers say Anthropic misled them into believing they’d get more out of a top-tier pricing subscription than they did.

In an expanded class action lawsuit filed today, a group of Claude subscribers say the company deceptively advertised the limits of its Max subscription tier. The lawsuit was brought by attorneys Monica Vaca and Kati Daffan, who both formerly worked at the Federal Trade Commission under Lina Khan. It’s a rare attempt to legally penalize AI companies for a widely held point of frustration: the industry’s growing money squeeze.

Anthropic’s Max plan for Claude is an upgrade to the $20/month Pro plan. It has two pricing options: $100 per month for “5x” the usage limits of Pro or $200 per month for “20x”. But the lawsuit alleges that these numbers, advertised in Anthropic’s marketing graphics, are misleadingly couched in fine print. Anthropic actually says you’ll get 20x or 5x the usage that the Pro plan offers, but it’s only promised for five-hour chunks of time that are subject to a weekly limit — which the complaint alleges adds up to a much smaller total increase in usage capacity.

To understand this, “you’ve got to dive deep,” Vaca said. It requires clicking two different hyperlinks to see the word “session,” and then to see what “session” meant, you’d need to separately go to the Pro plan webpage for an expanded definition.

Complaints about Max’s terms have cropped up online. One Reddit user wrote, “The weekly allowance is what the pricing page makes you think you’re buying. The rolling 5-hour window is what actually controls whether you can work … It’s like giving someone a bigger gas tank while keeping the fuel pump limited to one gallon every five hours.”

Vaca said in an interview that Claude users often will upgrade on the fly if they encounter limits while working on a project, then are often frustrated after they pay. “People see that they are going to get this dramatically expanded usage … What we hear from people, though, is that when they sign up, they are surprised that they’re not getting the usage that they thought they were getting.”

Over the past eight months or more, as pressures to turn a profit increase, AI customers have frequently complained that top labs are passing on their steep operating costs. Although Anthropic announced the Max plan in April 2025, it didn’t impose the allegedly deceptive weekly limits until a few months later in August, as the company pushed to compete with OpenAI. In Anthropic’s latest model release, Fable 5.1, the company hinted at broader cost concerns among customers, writing that it was “addressing the feedback we’ve received from customers on price” in the new model’s pricing.

The complaint was filed in July before being withdrawn and refiled as an expanded class action. In a motion to dismiss the earlier case, Anthropic argued that it didn’t necessarily omit the session limits from its marketing; rather, it says it’s technically available to the consumer if they know where to look. “Accessing this clarifying information … required nothing more than clicking hyperlinks available in the purchase process—the digital equivalent of flipping a product over to read the back label,” Anthropic wrote in the motion to dismiss.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment.

Vaca disagrees that it’s that easy to understand the terms. “This is hard for consumers — they don’t know what’s in that black box,” she said. “They have to rely on the claims the marketer is giving. There’s no way for them to audit it. There’s no way for them to know exactly what it is they’re going to get… They’re basically taking a leap, and they’re believing in an honest marketplace.”

She added that another reason the case was “compelling” for her is that she and Daffan started hearing from people who felt they needed to pay high-priced subscription costs for AI services in order to avoid becoming irrelevant in the job market. But oftentimes, she said, they felt they weren’t getting what they paid for, which was frustrating for a service that costs between $100 and $200 per month.

“[Daffan] and I worked at the Federal Trade Commission for 38 years combined,” Vaca said, adding, “There is a long line of precedent on false advertising. It’s commercial speech. You can’t lie when you’re marketing a product.”
Even if Anthropic has the stipulations somewhere on its website, Vaca said, it shouldn’t be up to the consumer to have to seek that out.
“It’s a ‘buyer beware’ approach,” she said. “And that’s really not fair to people.”

在今天提起的扩大集体诉讼中，一群Claude订阅者表示，该公司欺骗性地宣传了其Max订阅级别的限制。该诉讼由莫妮卡·瓦卡（ Monica Vaca ）和卡蒂·达凡（ Kati Daffan ）两名律师提起，他们都曾在莉娜·汗（ Lina Khan ）领导的联邦贸易委员会工作。这是一次罕见的尝试，试图以一种普遍存在的挫败感对AI公司进行法律惩罚：该行业不断增长的资金挤压。
Anthropic的Claude Max计划是对每月20美元的Pro计划的升级。它有两种定价选项： “5x”使用限额为每月100美元， “20x”使用限额为每月200美元。但该诉讼声称，在Anthropic的营销图片中宣传的这些数字具有误导性。Anthropic实际上表示您将获得Pro计划提供的20倍或5倍的使用量，但它只承诺每周限制五小时的时间—投诉声称这相当于使用容量的总增加量要小得多。
为了理解这一点， Vaca说： “你必须深入研究。”它需要单击两个不同的超链接才能看到“会话”一词，然后要查看“会话”的含义，您需要单独转到Pro计划网页以获取扩展定义。
网上出现了有关Max条款的投诉。一位Reddit用户写道： “每周津贴是定价页面让你认为你正在购买的东西。滚动的5小时窗口实际上控制着你是否可以工作……这就像给某人一个更大的油箱，同时将燃油泵限制在每五个小时一加仑。”
Vaca在接受采访时表示，如果Claude用户在开展项目时遇到限制，他们通常会即时升级，然后在付款后往往会感到沮丧。“人们看到他们将获得这种急剧扩大的使用……但我们从人们那里听到的是，当他们注册时，他们惊讶于他们没有得到他们认为他们得到的使用。”

在过去的八个月或更长时间里，随着扭亏为盈的压力增加，人工智能客户经常抱怨顶级实验室正在转嫁其高昂的运营成本。尽管Anthropic在2025年4月宣布了MAX计划，但直到8月份的几个月后，该公司才推出据称具有欺骗性的每周限制，因为该公司推动与OpenAI竞争。在Anthropic的最新车型版本Fable 5.1中，该公司暗示了客户对更广泛的成本担忧，并写道，它正在新车型的定价中“解决我们从客户那里收到的价格反馈”。
该投诉于7月提交，随后被撤回，并作为扩大的集体诉讼重新提起。在驳回早期案件的动议中， Anthropic辩称，它不一定会从其营销中省略会话限制；相反，它表示，如果他们知道在哪里寻找，它在技术上可以向消费者提供。Anthropic在驳回动议中写道： “访问这些澄清信息......只需要点击购买过程中可用的超链接-相当于将产品翻转过来阅读背面标签的数字链接。”
Anthropic没有回复置评请求。
Vaca不同意这些术语很容易理解的说法。“这对消费者来说很难—他们不知道黑匣子里有什么，”她说。“他们必须依靠营销人员给出的主张。他们没有办法审核。他们无法确切知道自己会得到什么……他们基本上是在飞跃，他们相信一个诚实的市场。”
她补充说，这个案子对她来说“引人注目”的另一个原因是，她和Daffan开始听到一些人认为他们需要支付高价的人工智能服务订阅费用，以避免在就业市场上变得无关紧要。但她说，很多时候，他们觉得自己没有得到他们付出的代价，这对于每月花费在100美元到200美元之间的服务来说是令人沮丧的。
“[Daffan]和我在联邦贸易委员会工作了38年，” Vaca说，并补充说， “虚假广告有一长串的先例。这是商业演讲。在营销产品时，你不能撒谎。”
Vaca说，即使Anthropic在其网站上的某个地方有这些规定，也不应该由消费者来寻求。
“这是一种‘买家小心’的方法，”她说。“这对人们来说真的不公平。”
